bib.title: Improving Neural Machine Translation Models with Monolingual Data
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), pages 86-96

question: Can NMT use target-side monolingual data during training, without changing the architecture, to improve translation quality?
hypothesis: Monolingual target data improves the estimate of p(T), and should help most when parallel data is sparse or domain-mismatched; the encoder-decoder already has capacity to learn LM information.
contributions: mixing monolingual target sentences into the training set improves NMT quality
two ways to fill the source side: dummy source sentence, or synthetic source via back-translation; the latter is more effective
adapt NMT models to a new domain by fine-tuning with monolingual or parallel in-domain data

method.summary: Target-language monolingual sentences are back-translated into the source language with an existing target-to-source NMT system, and the (synthetic source, real target) pairs are mixed 1-to-1 with the real parallel data and trained on with no architecture change. Compared to a dummy <null> source with frozen encoder/attention on monolingual batches.
method.task: neural machine translation (EN-DE, DE-EN, TR-EN), data augmentation with monolingual data

datasets.name: IWSLT 14 Turkish-English (WIT + SETimes)
datasets.size: 160 000 WIT + 160 000 SETimes; 320 000 pairs after filtering empty lines and length ratio above 9
datasets.split: tst2010 dev with early stopping; test tst2011-2014
datasets.source: Cettolo et al. 2014; Tyers and Alperen 2010
datasets.preprocessing: Zemberek morphological segmentation; rare morphemes as character bigram sequences; 20 000 most frequent left unsegmented; vocab 23 000

models.name: Bahdanau et al. attentional encoder-decoder (Groundhog)
models.architecture: bidirectional GRU encoder, GRU decoder with single-layer feedforward alignment model
models.tokenizer: BPE (joint, 89 500 merges) for EN-DE; character bigram for TR-EN

other.fixed_vocab: network vocabulary fixed from parallel data in all experiments
other.ensembles: EN-DE ens-4 sampled from last 4 saved models of one run (12h intervals); ens-3/ens-12 across runs

training.objective: maximum likelihood on parallel + monolingual/synthetic pairs, mixed 1-to-1 and shuffled; for dummy-source monolingual minibatches encoder and attention parameters are frozen; with synthetic data nothing is frozen
training.optimizer: stochastic gradient descent (otherwise 'follow settings of Sennrich et al. 2016')
training.epochs: epoch = one pass over parallel data, monolingual resampled each epoch
training.regularisation: TR-EN: Gaussian noise stddev 0.01, output dropout 0.5, early stopping on tst2010 BLEU every 3 hours
training.hardware: back-translation on one NVIDIA Titan Black GPU
training.compute: EN-DE baseline trained one week; back-translating 3.6M sentences took about a week
training.wall_clock: baseline 1 week; +monolingual trained twice as long; ensembles fine-tuned 12h with fixed embeddings

other.finetune: word embeddings fixed during domain fine-tuning; 1 epoch on WITsynth
other.backtranslation_models: DE-EN baseline (parallel), single model not ensemble, beam 12; EN-DE back-translation for DE-EN used the EN-DE +synthetic system; EN-TR system same settings as TR-EN baseline

inference.decoding: beam search; beam 12 for back-translation (greedy compared); small beam otherwise
inference.samples: single run per system; no seeds reported

parameters.mono_to_parallel_ratio: 1-to-1 (higher ratios decreased BLEU for dummy source)

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: EN-DE: case-sensitive BLEU on detokenized text, mteval-v13a.pl; TR-EN: case-sensitive tokenized BLEU, multi-bleu.perl

metrics.name: word naturalness
metrics.definition: words made from subword units not in parallel training data; share attested in monolingual corpus or reference, and share judged natural by one native speaker on random n=100 per system

eval.protocol: single training runs, no significance test or seeds; ensembles of 4 from one run unless stated

availability.code: uses Groundhog (github.com/sebastien-j/LV_groundhog); no release of the authors' code stated
availability.data: WMT, IWSLT, News Crawl and LDC Gigaword (public/licensed)

evidence.quote: We also experimented with higher ratios of monolingual data, but this led to decreased BLEU scores.

results.claim: Back-translated synthetic data improves EN to DE single-model BLEU on newstest2015 over the parallel baseline
results.setup: English to German, WMT 15, Groundhog attentional GRU encoder-decoder, BPE 89 500 merges, single models, newstest2014/2015, detokenized case-sensitive BLEU; 44m parallel + 36m synthetic instances

results.claim: Back-translation gives +2.8 to 3.4 BLEU over baseline for EN to DE
results.setup: English to German, WMT 15, Groundhog attentional GRU encoder-decoder, BPE 89 500 merges, single models, newstest2014/2015, detokenized case-sensitive BLEU
results.quote: yields an improvement over our baseline by 2.8–3.4 BLEU

results.claim: DE to EN gains 3.6-3.7 BLEU from synthetic source data, larger than deep fusion
results.setup: German to English WMT 15; EN back-translated with EN-DE +synthetic system
results.quote: substantial improvements (3.6–3.7 BLEU) from adding monolingual training data with synthetic source sentences

results.claim: DE to EN newstest2015 single model parallel vs +synthetic
results.setup: German to English WMT 15 single model

results.claim: Turkish to English gains 2.7 BLEU on average with Gigaword synthetic data, 0.5 over fusion
results.setup: IWSLT 14 TR-EN, 320k parallel + 3.2M synthetic, avg over tst2011-2014, tokenized BLEU, single models
results.quote: we outperform the baseline by 2.7 BLEU on average

results.claim: Dummy-source monolingual data gives smaller gain: 0.4-0.5 BLEU single, 1 BLEU ensemble for EN to DE
results.setup: English to German, WMT 15, Groundhog attentional GRU encoder-decoder, BPE 89 500 merges, single models, newstest2014/2015, detokenized case-sensitive BLEU; ratio 1-1, trained twice as long
results.quote: improves quality by 0.4–0.5 BLEU for the single system, 1 BLEU for the ensemble

results.claim: Continuing baseline training another week gave no BLEU improvement (control for training time)
results.setup: English to German, WMT 15, Groundhog attentional GRU encoder-decoder, BPE 89 500 merges, single models, newstest2014/2015, detokenized case-sensitive BLEU

results.claim: Fine-tuning one epoch on back-translated in-domain WIT monolingual data gives +1.2 BLEU on tst2015 (TED)
results.setup: EN to DE, WMT-trained system 2 adapted to TED; WITsynth 200k; embeddings fixed

results.claim: Fine-tuning on in-domain WIT parallel data gives 28.4 on tst2015 (+2.9)
results.setup: EN to DE TED adaptation, 200k WIT parallel

results.claim: Fine-tuning on monolingual TED with dummy input gave no improvement
results.setup: EN to DE TED adaptation, system 3

results.claim: 6 BLEU difference in back-translation quality gives only 0.6-0.7 BLEU difference in final EN to DE quality
results.setup: DE to EN back-translators: greedy vs beam 12 vs synthetic-trained; EN to DE newstest2015
results.quote: leads to a 0.6–0.7 BLEU difference in translation quality

results.claim: Ensembles of independently trained systems add 0.8-1.0 BLEU over 4 checkpoints from one run
results.setup: EN to DE, ensemble of 3/12 across runs

results.claim: Back-translation helps NMT more than phrase-based SMT on WMT test sets (+2.9 vs +0.7) and IWSLT (+1.2 vs +0.1)
results.setup: EN to DE, Moses with 5-gram KN LM on all WMT data; avg newstest2014/15 and tst2013-15
results.table: Table 8, rows PBSMT gain and NMT gain

results.claim: Parallel-only Turkish model overfits quickly; mono/synthetic data delay overfitting and Gigaword synthetic gives best dev cross-entropy
Novel subword-built words are more often natural with monolingual or synthetic data (parallel 74.9%, +mono 84.6%, +synthetic 82.5% natural)
results.setup: EN to DE newstest2015, ensembles, one native-speaker annotator, n=100 unattested words per system, blinded

results.claim: Synthetic parallel text from the same parallel corpus (parallelsynth) still helps TR-EN by 1.7 BLEU on average, less than novel Gigaword mono data in the synth variant

limits: Only a small random sample of the available monolingual data was used; larger or selected synthetic sets are untested.
Sensitivity to back-translation quality only tested via decoding variants; amount of synthetic data not varied.
Single runs, no seeds or significance tests; ensembles of 4 sampled from one run lack diversity.
Naturalness annotation is by one author, n=100 per system.
RNN attentional GRU architecture from 2015; no Transformer.
Dummy-source method cannot raise the monolingual ratio without unlearning source conditioning.
Learning rate, batch size, hidden sizes and epoch counts are not stated here (deferred to Sennrich et al. 2016).

terms.definition: an automatic translation of the monolingual target text into the source language
source sentence obtained via back-translation, paired with a real target sentence
